content.user_title: Add Object Storage to Caffeine AI Apps
content.value_statement: Large files need storage beyond Internet Computer canister limits. This skill guides Caffeine AI projects through backend integration, browser uploads, cached display, downloads, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Configures required mops and npm dependencies for object storage.
Integrates MixinObjectStorage and Storage.ExternalBlob into a Motoko actor.
Creates browser upload flows with MIME type, filename, and progress metadata.
Produces direct display URLs and byte-based downloads through ExternalBlob.
Diagnoses common 403 payload failures and incorrect backend method signatures.
limitations: Applies to Caffeine AI projects using the documented Motoko and TypeScript packages.
Does not provide authentication, authorization, quotas, malware scanning, or content moderation.
Depends on off-chain gateway availability and external package versions selected by the project.
Does not define retention, deletion, backup, privacy, or regulatory compliance policies.

use_cases.title: Build a media gallery
use_cases.description: Add image and video uploads, cached display, progress reporting, and persistent file metadata.

use_cases.title: Deliver stored documents
use_cases.description: Create inline previews and named downloads from ExternalBlob records without storing file bytes in canisters.

use_cases.title: Repair failed uploads
use_cases.description: Trace 403 responses to missing dependencies, absent mixins, incorrect data types, or invalid reserved method signatures.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Caffeine AI project and list the required backend and frontend steps for object storage. Identify files that need changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a first object storage integration

prompt_templates.title: Create an upload flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an upload flow using ExternalBlob.fromBytes with filename, MIME type, and progress. Store the ExternalBlob reference in my Motoko record.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adding browser uploads to an existing application

prompt_templates.title: Add display and download
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement inline media display with getDirectURL and named downloads with getBytes. Use stored MIME type or filename for file classification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Building file viewing and retrieval features

prompt_templates.title: Audit the integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my object storage integration for dependency, type, mixin, signature, and gateway errors. Explain each problem and propose precise corrections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnosing a complex or failing implementation

output_examples.input: Set up object storage for an image gallery.
output: Backend: add the mops dependency and include the storage mixin in the main actor.
Data model: store each image as ExternalBlob with filename and MIME type.
Frontend: convert selected files to bytes, upload with progress, and render cached direct URLs.

output_examples.input: Explain why every upload returns a 403 payload error.
output_examples.output: The backend package or storage mixin is probably missing. Verify both dependencies, remove custom reserved methods, rebuild, and redeploy the backend.
Use direct URLs for inline viewing. Fetch bytes for named downloads, preserve stored filenames, and revoke temporary browser URLs after use.

best_practices: Store file references as Storage.ExternalBlob and retain filename plus MIME type as separate metadata.
Install compatible backend and frontend packages together, then rebuild and redeploy after backend changes.
Use direct URLs for inline media and byte downloads when the original filename must be preserved.
anti_patterns: Do not store object references as text or implement reserved storage methods manually.
Do not infer media types from opaque gateway URLs.
Do not accept arbitrary uploads without application-level authorization, validation, size limits, and content controls.

faq.question: Where are uploaded file bytes stored?
faq.answer: File content is stored off-chain. The Motoko backend stores ExternalBlob references and application metadata.

faq.question: Which dependencies are required?
faq.answer: Install caffeineai-object-storage through mops and @caffeineai/object-storage through npm. Both packages are required.

faq.question: Can this handle large files?
faq.answer: The extension targets files beyond normal canister limits, subject to package, gateway, browser, and application constraints.

faq.question: Why do uploads return 403 Invalid payload?
faq.answer: Common causes include a missing backend package, an absent mixin, incorrect ExternalBlob types, or a custom reserved method.

faq.question: How should files be displayed or downloaded?
faq.answer: Use getDirectURL for inline display. Use getBytes for downloads that preserve the stored filename.

faq.question: Does the skill secure uploaded content?
faq.answer: No. Applications must add authorization, validation, size limits, malware controls, retention rules, and privacy safeguards.
